learn.hook: Every day in India, many thousands of babies are born. Some people pass away and some people move in or out. Together these decide how the population changes.
points: Population changes because of three things: births, deaths and migration (people moving into or out of a place).
The birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 people in a year. The death rate is the number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.
The natural growth rate is the birth rate minus the death rate. When births are more than deaths, the population grows.
Better health care, clean water and vaccines lowered death rates, so India's population grew fast in the 20th century. Birth rates have also been falling over time.

India counts its people through the Census, held every ten years. According to the Census of 2011, India had about 121 crore people. United Nations estimates show that India became the world's most populous country in 2023, overtaking China.

example.q: Think it through: A town has a birth rate of 20 per 1,000 and a death rate of 7 per 1,000. What is its natural growth rate?
steps: Natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate.
So the town grows by 13 people per 1,000 each year, not counting migration.

learn.reallife: Census officials visit every home, even in remote villages and islands, to count each person. The data helps the government plan schools, hospitals and roads.

games.title: True or false?
items: Population changes through births, deaths and migration.
These three factors decide population change.
The natural growth rate is the birth rate plus the death rate.
It is the birth rate minus the death rate.
The Census of India is held every ten years.
Lower death rates were a big reason for India's population growth in the 20th century.
Better health care meant fewer deaths while birth rates stayed high for a long time.
Migration means the number of babies born.
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another.

quiz.q: Which three factors change the population of a place?
quiz.explain: People are added by births and in-migration and lost by deaths and out-migration.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the components of population change

quiz.q: The birth rate is the number of live births per:
quiz.explain: Birth rate is measured per 1,000 people per year.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how the rate is measured

quiz.q: A village has a birth rate of 24 and a death rate of 9 per 1,000. What is its natural growth rate per 1,000?
steps: Natural growth = birth rate − death rate

quiz.q: How often is the Census held in India?
quiz.explain: The Census is held once in ten years.

quiz.q: According to the Census of 2011, India's population was about:
quiz.explain: The 2011 Census counted about 121 crore (1.21 billion) people.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up crore and lakh scales

quiz.q: Which country did India overtake in 2023 to become the most populous, according to UN estimates?
quiz.explain: UN estimates show India passed China in 2023.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the world's most populous countries

quiz.q: Why did India's population grow quickly in the 20th century?
options: Death rates fell sharply due to better health care, while birth rates stayed high for long
quiz.explain: Falling deaths with high births cause rapid growth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks growth happens only because of more births

quiz.q: When people move out of a village to a city for work, the village population changes because of:
quiz.explain: Out-migration reduces the population of the village.

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why his forest has more birds every year. Explain how populations grow.
teach.praise: Births add, deaths subtract, and migration moves birds around. My forest makes sense now!
teach.nudge: What adds to a population, and what reduces it? What is natural growth?

learn.hook: Some parts of India are packed with people, while in parts of Ladakh you may travel for hours without seeing a house. Why?
points: Population distribution means how people are spread over an area. In India and the world, it is very uneven.
Population density is the number of people living per square kilometre. Density = total population ÷ area. According to the Census of 2011, India's density was 382 people per sq km.
Physical factors affect distribution: flat land, fertile soil, a pleasant climate and water attract people. Mountains, deserts, thick forests and very cold or very hot places have few people.
Economic and social factors matter too: jobs in industries and cities, minerals, transport, and services like schools and hospitals draw people.

The Ganga plains and coastal plains are densely populated. The Thar Desert, the high Himalayas and Ladakh are thinly populated. In the 2011 Census, Bihar had the highest density among the states and Arunachal Pradesh the lowest.

example.q: Think it through: A district has 6,00,000 people and an area of 1,500 sq km. What is its population density?
steps: So 400 people live in each square kilometre on average.

learn.reallife: Kolkata, Patna and Lucknow on the fertile Ganga plains are crowded, while hill towns in Arunachal Pradesh are small and spread out.

items.text: Density is measured in people per square ___.
In the 2011 Census, India's density was ___ people per sq km.
Among states, ___ had the highest density in 2011.

quiz.q: What is population density?
options: The number of births per year
The number of people per square kilometre
The height of a city's buildings
quiz.explain: Density tells how crowded a place is.

quiz.q: A town has 50,000 people in an area of 100 sq km. What is its density in people per sq km?
According to the Census of 2011, India's population density in people per sq km was:
quiz.explain: India had 382 people per sq km in 2011.

quiz.q: Which region of India is densely populated?
quiz.explain: Fertile soil, water and flat land attract many people.
quiz.mistake: Does not link physical factors with population

quiz.q: Why do few people live in the Thar Desert?
options: There is little water and the climate is very harsh
It is too cold all year
quiz.explain: Lack of water limits farming and settlement.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the features of deserts

quiz.q: In the 2011 Census, which state had the lowest population density?
quiz.explain: Its steep hills and thick forests support few people per sq km.

quiz.q: Which of these is an economic factor that attracts people to a place?
quiz.explain: People move to where they can find work.

quiz.q: Region A has 2,000 people on 10 sq km. Region B has 3,000 people on 30 sq km. Which is more densely populated?
quiz.mistake: Compares total population instead of density

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a big country always has a crowded population. Explain distribution and density to Gappu.
teach.praise: So density is people per square kilometre, and water, soil and jobs decide where people live!
teach.nudge: What is density and how do we calculate it? Why are some places crowded and others empty?

topics.title: Population composition: people as a resource

learn.hook: Two towns have the same number of people. In one, most are children; in the other, most are grandparents. Would their needs be the same?
points: Population composition describes the make-up of a population by age, sex, literacy, occupation and where people live.
By age, people are grouped as children, working-age adults and the elderly. Children and the elderly depend on working-age people.
The sex ratio is the number of females per 1,000 males. According to the Census of 2011, India's sex ratio was 943, and Kerala had the highest among the states.
A population pyramid is a graph that shows how many males and females are in each age group. A wide base means many children.
India has a large share of young people. If they are healthy, educated and skilled, they can become a huge strength for the country. This is called the demographic dividend.

example.q: Think it through: A village has 450 females and 500 males. What is its sex ratio?

learn.reallife: Programmes like Skill India and the push for girls' education aim to turn India's young population into a skilled workforce.

games.title: Match the term
pairs: Graph of age and sex groups
Benefit from a large working-age population

quiz.q: What does the sex ratio measure?
options: The number of males per 100 females
The number of births per year
The number of females per 1,000 males
The number of children per family
quiz.explain: India measures sex ratio as females per 1,000 males.

quiz.q: According to the Census of 2011, India's sex ratio was:
quiz.explain: There were 943 females per 1,000 males in 2011.

quiz.q: Which state had the highest sex ratio in the 2011 Census?
quiz.explain: Kerala had more females than males.

quiz.q: A town has 960 females and 1,000 males. What is its sex ratio?
quiz.explain: 960 females per 1,000 males gives a sex ratio of 960.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of reading the ratio

quiz.q: A population pyramid with a very wide base shows:
options: Equal numbers in every age group
quiz.explain: The base of the pyramid shows the youngest age groups.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to read a population pyramid

quiz.q: Which group is usually called 'dependent'?
quiz.explain: They usually depend on working-age people for support.

quiz.q: What is the 'demographic dividend'?
options: Money paid by the Census office
The benefit a country can gain from a large, skilled working-age population
quiz.explain: Young, skilled workers can boost the economy.

quiz.q: Why does a population with many children need more schools?
options: Children need education, so demand for schools rises
The number of children does not matter
quiz.explain: Composition tells planners what services are needed.
quiz.mistake: Does not link population make-up with planning

teach.ask: Gappu thinks counting people is enough. Explain why the make-up of a population matters.
teach.praise: So we need to know who the people are, not just how many! Gappu will plan more nests for chicks.
teach.nudge: What does population composition tell us? What is the sex ratio, and why do young people matter?
